title: Brookies (Brownie and Cookie Bars)
summary: Fudgy brownie batter topped with patches of chocolate chip cookie dough, baked together into one big tray of bars.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm metal baking tin (not glass), lined with a baking-paper sling
heatproof bowl over a pan of barely simmering water

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled until warm
fine sea salt or table salt
dark chocolate chips or chunks (50-60% cocoa solids)

steps.title: Heat oven, line tin
steps.text: Heat the oven to 175°C (155°C fan) for at least 20 minutes before baking. Line the 23x33cm metal tin with a baking-paper sling so both layers lift out together once baked.

steps.title: Make the brownie layer
steps.text: Melt the chocolate and butter together over a pan of barely simmering water, then take off the heat and whisk in the sugar, followed by the eggs one at a time and the vanilla, until glossy. Fold in the flour, cocoa and salt just until combined, then spread this batter evenly in the tin as the dense base.

steps.title: Make the cookie layer
steps.text: Whisk the warm melted butter with both sugars, then beat in the egg and vanilla. Fold in the flour, bicarbonate of soda, salt and chocolate chips to make a soft dough; this layer stays chunkier so it bakes up with distinct cookie edges rather than melting into the brownie.

steps.title: Assemble the layers
steps.text: Drop spoonfuls of the cookie dough over the brownie batter and press gently into an even patchwork, leaving some gaps. Those gaps let the fudgy brownie layer show through once baked, giving every square a mix of textures.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake for 28-32 minutes, until the cookie dough is golden at the edges and the brownie layer looks glossy. A skewer pushed into the centre should come out with a few moist crumbs rather than wet batter.

steps.title: Cool and cut
steps.text: Cool completely in the tin, about 1 hour, before cutting into 24 bars. Cutting while still warm will drag the soft brownie layer and smear the layers together.

tips: Leave gaps between the dollops of cookie dough rather than covering the brownie layer completely — the exposed brownie is what gives brookies their marbled look once baked.
Check with a skewer in the centre rather than at the edges; the middle needs those moist crumbs to confirm it's cooked through.
Let the tin cool fully before cutting, or the warm brownie layer will smear under the knife instead of slicing cleanly.
Add the eggs to the brownie mixture one at a time off the heat, so the warm chocolate doesn't scramble them.
Don't taste the raw dough or batter: raw flour and raw egg aren't safe to eat until baked.
storage: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 4 days, or freeze the cut bars for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature, or warm briefly, before eating.
